weakest_line: But death was only the first thing to change.
one_fix: Anchor the speculation in one hard text detail (e.g. the tree of life in Genesis 3:22, the thing they actually lost access to) so there is a clear 'oh' answer instead of a mood piece capped by a C.S. Lewis quote.

weakest_line: So the next time someone asks you where Cain's wife came from, you'll know what to say.
one_fix: Cut the 'most Christians can't answer it' filler and the 'you'll know what to say' close; end on the 'one blood' idea with a real question to the viewer.

weakest_line: That's what he was warning them about.
one_fix: Drop the Peter detour (his denial isn't the sin in question) and spend that time making the Mark 3:30 reason land plainly: Jesus said it because they called the Spirit's work an unclean spirit.

weakest_line: So God gave us free will, and He tells us plainly which way to choose.
one_fix: Replace the hypothetical steal/covet argument with evidence from Genesis 2 itself (every other tree 'freely' given, the tree of life also standing there) so the answer is earned from the text, not reasoned around it.

weakest_line: People ask this in our comments all the time.
one_fix: Cut to the single strongest answer (Cornelius, stated accurately, since Acts 10:37 says he already knew of Jesus' ministry) and end with a real question instead of assuming the viewer is a Christian who was told about Jesus.
Cut the colleague-lie analogy and use the time on the Peter vs Judas contrast, which sets up the closing question directly.

weakest_line: Because it was the only thing standing between a family and death.
one_fix: Replace the familiar Exodus backstory with an actual answer: a lamb died in place of the firstborn ('when I see the blood, I will pass over you', Exodus 12:13), then connect it to Christ as the Passover lamb (1 Corinthians 5:7).

weakest_line: And if you're here to stand for God's word, welcome to the Valiant.
one_fix: Trim the stack of authorities (Schellenberg, Kierkegaard, Pascal) to one so the argument lands on a single listen, and drop the branding tag after the question.

Open with the real puzzle (why would God ask Adam 'Where art thou?' if He already knew?) instead of a devotional question aimed at 'we', and cut the sermon-style lines that assume the viewer is hiding.

weakest_line: Some Christians also wonder about this question sometimes.
one_fix: Actually address the 'forever' part of the hook with text instead of stacking familiar verses, and drop the mislabeled 'how the Bible ends' (Revelation 3:20 is not the end) and 'the enemy wants you lost' preaching.
